docs.purpose: Tracks every development session on Sorriva. Used by the Velocity Dashboard to calculate development velocity, estimated cost savings vs traditional development, and cumulative AI-assisted hours. Also provides a historical record of what shipped when.
docs.blended_rate: Hourly rate in USD representing what a traditional developer would charge for equivalent work. Used to calculate cost savings vs AI-assisted development. Set to $170/hr — a blended rate for senior full-stack + design + product work in the US market.
docs.claude_monthly_cost: Monthly subscription cost of Claude in USD. Used to calculate ROI: (estimated_hours * blended_rate) / claude_monthly_cost.
docs.duration_hrs: Equivalent traditional developer hours for the session — NOT the user's actual time or wall-clock time. Represents how long a senior human developer (or team) would have taken to design, build, test, and ship the same scope of work. Calculated by summing the complexity-hour values of all features shipped: XS=3hrs, S=8hrs, M=20hrs, L=40hrs, XL=80hrs. For planning/architecture sessions with no features shipped, duration_hrs is set manually based on equivalent analyst/architect/product time for the scope of work produced.
docs.estimated: Boolean. true = duration_hrs was computed from complexity ratings of features_shipped or manually estimated for planning sessions. false = duration_hrs was set manually with high confidence. owner_hrs is never estimated — always user-reported.
docs.features_shipped: Array of roadmap feature IDs (e.g. fLibraryScanner) shipped in this session. Cross-references roadmap-data.json for complexity, phase, and description.
docs.version: The app version at the end of this session. Matches version.json.
session_close_checklist: 1. Mark completed roadmap features as done=true in roadmap-data.json
2. PROMPT USER: 'How many hours did you personally spend on this session?' Record answer as owner_hrs. Do not estimate — must come from the user.

3. Append session entry to sessions.json: session_id (YYYY-MM-DD-N), date, duration_hrs (sum of complexity hours for features shipped, or manual estimate for planning sessions), owner_hrs (user-reported), estimated, version, features_shipped, notes
4. Update sorriva-handoff.html — bump version, update current state, next priorities
5. Build final deploy zip: app.py (if changed), frontend HTML, handoff, roadmap-data.json, sessions.json
docs.velocity_dashboard_fields: The Velocity Dashboard will compute: total_duration_hrs (sum of all duration_hrs — equivalent traditional dev hours), total_owner_hrs (sum of all owner_hrs — user's actual time invested), estimated_cost_savings (total_duration_hrs * blended_rate), roi_multiple (estimated_cost_savings / cumulative_claude_cost), avg_duration_hrs_per_session, avg_owner_hrs_per_session, leverage_ratio (duration_hrs / owner_hrs per session — how many equiv dev hours per hour of user time), features_per_session, and a timeline chart of cumulative equivalent hours and savings by version.
docs.owner_hrs: Tom's actual hours spent in the session — reported by the user at session close. Never estimated by Claude. Represents time as product owner, solutions architect, QA, and domain expert. Null if the user did not report before session closed. At session close, Claude must ask: 'How many hours did you personally spend on this session?' and record the answer here before finalizing.
docs.session_id: Unique identifier for each session. Format: YYYY-MM-DD-N where N is a 1-based sequence number for sessions on the same date (e.g. '2026-06-24-1', '2026-06-24-2'). Always increment N for each new session on the same day — check existing entries before appending to avoid collision.

notes: Session durations are estimated based on scope of work, features shipped, and complexity. Not wall-clock time — represents active development time equivalent. Sorriva is a pure App Store product — iOS/iPadOS primary, Apple TV Phase 6. No self-hosted server for app logic.

Architecture principles locked: zero hardcoded paths, env vars throughout, multi-instance ready, clean API separation (/api/v1/), service layer pattern, WebSocket for real-time, auth middleware stub, commercial-ready schema. 8-phase development plan defined. Deep product strategy and competitive analysis session — no code shipped. Major architectural discovery and revision around audio delivery. Key decisions locked: (1) AirPlay 2 demoted from primary audio backbone to fallback-only for cross-ecosystem groups and AirPlay-only devices. Connect protocols (Spotify Connect, Qobuz Connect, Tidal Connect) adopted as primary streaming delivery — device pulls stream directly from cloud, phone is controller only, full hi-res preserved. (2) Multi-room architecture clarified: Sonos zones grouped via Sonos HTTP API (native, any combination, 24/48 lossless), Bluesound zones grouped via BluOS API (native, any combination, 24/192 lossless), cross-ecosystem groups use AirPlay 2 fallback (16/44.1 lossless CD, honestly labelled). (3) Sorriva can do what Roon cannot: group Sonos + Bluesound together at CD quality via AirPlay 2 fallback — Roon refuses cross-ecosystem grouping entirely at any quality. 'Best quality or everywhere' framing locked as product positioning. (4) Audio quality architecture: nobody gets lossy audio in Sorriva except via Spotify (source limitation). Lossless on every path. Hi-res requires Bluesound hardware. Signal Path Indicator feature added — shows source format, delivery protocol, and endpoint quality at all times. (5) MQA: not building (MQA Ltd in administration 2023, industry abandoning format). (6) Per-device PCM/multichannel config not needed — handled automatically by device and protocol, server-model complexity eliminated. (7) Roon Ready demystified: RAAT requires Roon Core server, certification, and licensed hardware — Connect protocols deliver equivalent real-world quality without any of those dependencies. Four new reference documents produced: sorriva-competitive.html (competitive matrix vs Roon, 11 Sorriva advantages), sorriva-product-spec.html (full feature reference, 10 product areas, Audio Quality Positioning section), sorriva-audio-quality.html (lossless vs hi-res explainer, streaming service quality table, delivery path matrix, hardware quality table). All docs in Sorriva brand system, internally consistent. Consumer education positioning locked: 'The market conflates lossless and hi-res. Scanner metadata defect session. Root cause found for compilation tracks being written to the database as "Various Artists": SMBScanner resolved a single artist from meta.albumArtist ?? meta.artist and used it for both the album and the track, so ALBUMARTIST always won and a track could not structurally differ from its album. Fixed by resolving albumArtist and trackArtist independently with correct precedence — ALBUMARTIST governs the album, ARTIST governs the track, each falling back to the other only when absent. Track and upsertTrackArtist now write the track artist. No migration required: Track already carried its own primaryArtistId and artistName. resolveArtist normalized to match on a trimmed, case-folded key while preserving original display casing, with a new case-insensitive artist(namedNormalized:) lookup in SorrivaDatabase so variants resolve to one artist row across scans and not just within a single scan cache. Removed the title plus artist fallback from resolveAlbum, making folderPath the sole album deduplication key — the fallback merged two folders into one album whenever their ALBUM tags matched, which the data on disk never asserts, and since every compilation resolves to the same Various Artists row any two compilations sharing an ALBUM tag collapsed into a single album. LibraryService.listArtists now filters VA, Various, and Various Artists from artist browse while leaving the rows and album relationships intact, so album views still show the compilation artist. Investigation also confirmed: tag parsing correctly handles the non-standard YEAR field written by Windows Media Player rips; the 64KB tag read and separate 1MB embedded art pass are working as designed; the disc-collapse regex in fillFromPath never fires against this library because every disc folder carries a full album name rather than a bare Disc N; and the v13 canonical tables inherited the wrong artist IDs in their backfill but are dormant, since SourceResolver maps through LegacyMusicMapper from the live legacy Track row. THE CAUSE: SMBClient v0.3.1 never calls NWConnection.cancel() anywhere. Session.disconnect() -> connection.disconnect() -> cancel() exists, but nothing in the library calls it; the only occurrence of .disconnect() in the source is its own definition. SMBClient exposes no public wrapper, and there is no deinit on Connection, Session, or SMBClient. logoff() sends the SMB2 LOGOFF frame and zeroes sessionId while leaving the TCP connection open, so every file read leaked a kernel flow entry against a hard per-process ceiling of exactly 512. A prior session's note claiming that chain had been 'verified in SMBClient's source' was wrong, and ScanCoordinator.swift still carries a comment asserting the same false thing.

THE FIX: client.session.disconnect() on all four teardown paths in SMBMediaSourceReader (walk close, auth failure, share failure, read success), and in the timeout handler INSTEAD of logoff() -- logoff() awaits a response on a connection that is hung by definition, so the call meant to break the hang could itself hang. No fork needed: `session` is public on SMBClient and Session.disconnect() is public.
